chunks: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

'When a man and a woman are found in one quilt, and proof is established against them both regarding that, and nothing else emerges from them besides that, each one of them shall be flogged one hundred lashes.'

key_terms.بَيِّنَةٌ: bayyinah — legal proof (typically two or more witnesses) sufficient to establish the act in court
key_terms.جُلِدَ: flogging/lashing — the physical punishment prescribed here
key_terms.لِحَافٍ: quilt/blanket — sharing one blanket with an unrelated person of the opposite sex is itself legally significant
key_terms.مِائَةَ جَلْدَةٍ: one hundred lashes — the prescribed count, the same as the hadd for zina in Quranic law (24:2)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling when a man and woman are found sharing a blanket with witnesses but no other act is proven?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) rules that if a man and an unrelated woman are found together under one blanket and this is legally witnessed, but no act beyond that is proven, each receives the ta'zir punishment of one hundred lashes. This ruling reflects the classical Shia jurisprudential principle that specific illicit acts short of zina (fornication) carry their own prescribed penalties when established by bayinnah (legal proof). The original audience — Shia jurists and scholars — would have understood this as a ruling distinguishing between zina (which requires four witnesses and carries a different hadd) and lesser violations of moral boundaries that still warrant a full hadd-like punishment of 100 lashes.

en.hubeali:
Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Sama’at, from someone else, from Aban and Muhammad Bin Yahya Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Abdullah having said: 
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said:

‘When the man and the woman are both found to be in one quilt, and the proof is established upon them with that, and nothing else emerges from them both besides that, each one of them would be whipped one hundred lashes’.
